proposed_from.topic: Develop and audit an effective fixed-separation minimax theory for non-Gaussian partially linear models using complex moment-generating-function zeros. Prove the exact learned-residual factorization and contour-identification identities; derive a numerical zero-localization radius from the exact Luxemburg sub-Gaussian convention; and construct an explicit once-for-all translated-dyadic uniformly conditioned contour bank with a positive dyadic modulus computable from certified-real names of the displayed primitive class constants, without access to the unknown treatment-noise law. Show that the resulting total certified split-sample statistic attains uniform Θ(n^{-1}) MSE under sufficiently small fixed direct L^1(P_X) treatment-code error without an outcome learner. Retain the exact Jin–Mackey–Syrgkanis Theorem 5.4 ACE upper comparison only on the explicit narrower comparison subclass. Treat the bounded-Y Gaussian calculation solely as a source-assumption diagnostic showing that the simultaneous assumptions stated around their Theorem 3.2 force θ_0=0, not as a Gaussian-versus-non-Gaussian minimax dichotomy. Leave the shrinking-separation phase diagram, adaptive switching, uniform inference, and matching local lower bounds open. Position the effective fixed-separation result narrowly against higher-order OML, location-family completeness and zero testing, spectral GMM, ICA treatment-effect estimation, and weak-non-Gaussian inference without claiming that transform zeros themselves are new.
proposed_from.novelty_justification: The closest theorem-level comparator is \cite[Theorem 5.4, condition (21), and bound (22)]{JinMackeySyrgkanis2025}. On its eligible class intersection, the published ACE generalized-quantile guarantee retains \(\varepsilon_{1,n}^r\varepsilon_{2,n}+C_{\theta}\varepsilon_{1,n}^{r+1}\); the proposed exact contour estimator targets uniform MSE \(\Theta(n^{-1})\) for \(\varepsilon_{1,n}\le\varepsilon_0\), including fixed nonzero error, and does not use the outcome code or know the noise law. The transform-zero idea itself is not claimed as new. The claimed advance is its PLM nuisance-annihilation use, stability under learned-residual contamination, observable adaptation to unknown noise through a finite contour bank, and the resulting minimax implication.

anchor_paper.locator: Introduction, Gaussian treatment-barrier theorem, sub-Gaussian ACE theorem, and Conclusion
anchor_paper.open_question: The paper resolves Gaussian optimality and gives finite-order non-Gaussian improvements, but it does not determine whether the non-Gaussian nuisance terms are minimax or whether an exact-transform procedure removes them.

seed_details.red_team: A cynical referee may call the result immediate by sending the ACE order to infinity.
seed_details.rebuttal: ACE constants and identifying cumulants vary with order, while the contour score annihilates every shift exactly at one fixed class and yields a finite unknown-noise estimator; no limit of the published finite-order theorem gives the uniform bank or fixed-error root-\(n\) claim.
seed_details.closest_result: JinMackeySyrgkanis2025, Gaussian barrier theorem and sub-Gaussian ACE theorem
seed_details.precise_gap: The published non-Gaussian upper bound retains \(\varepsilon_1^r\varepsilon_2+C_{\theta}\varepsilon_1^{r+1}\); no theorem gives uniform \(n^{-1}\) mean-squared error at fixed nonzero \(\varepsilon_1\) without an outcome learner.

anchor_paper.locator: Introduction's Gaussian versus non-Gaussian question, ACE strength discussion, and Conclusion
anchor_paper.open_question: The fixed-law split leaves open the triangular regime in which non-Gaussian information vanishes and the useful transform zero recedes.

seed_details.red_team: The phase transition may be a routine substitution of \(\delta_n\) into the fixed-separation constant.
seed_details.rebuttal: Cumulant size, nearest-zero radius, contour boundary modulus, exponential variance, and nuisance contamination need not be equivalent locally; matching lower experiments and a regime-adaptive procedure require new analytic inequalities.
seed_details.precise_gap: No PLM minimax result interpolates among DML, ACE, and spectral estimation as non-Gaussian strength shrinks.
seed_details.step1_status: survives as the first-class open extension but is not selected as the proved kernel

anchor_paper.locator: Introduction, Theorem 3.1 on an isolated first zero, empirical application, and Conclusion
anchor_paper.open_question: The paper's zero procedure is pointwise and its Conclusion explains why uniform testing fails over broad unseparated classes; complex contours with learned residuals and multiple zeros remain untreated.

seed_details.red_team: Conditional on a pilot-selected contour, an ordinary delta method may make the confidence interval routine.
seed_details.rebuttal: Selection need not stabilize near tied contours or multiple zeros, and uniform coverage requires foldwise studentization, variance nondegeneracy, measurable fallback, and control of wrong winding counts at the coverage scale.
seed_details.precise_gap: Existing empirical-characteristic-function zero theory is real-axis and pointwise, not selection-uniform inference for a causal contour ratio built from learned residuals.

anchor_paper.locator: Introduction, efficiency results for expected conditional covariance, and discussion of split-specific efficiency
anchor_paper.open_question: Cross-fitting isolates nuisance remainders, but no efficiency theory chooses among multiple complex annihilating moments after learning the residual law.

seed_details.red_team: Once contours are stacked as real GMM moments, Hansen efficiency may settle the answer immediately.
seed_details.rebuttal: The moment set and its dimension are themselves law-dependent through transform zeros, so deriving the tangent-space bound and proving adaptive contour aggregation attains it are not standard fixed-moment GMM.
seed_details.precise_gap: No efficiency bound or attaining aggregation exists for a PLM identified by an unknown finite bank of complex location-family annihilators.
seed_details.step1_status: credible but deferred because the fixed-separation minimax claim is sharper and directly supported

proposed_from.literature_map: Three candidates survived deepening. For the selected dichotomy, \cite{JinMackeySyrgkanis2025}, Introduction, Gaussian treatment-barrier theorem, sub-Gaussian ACE theorem, and Conclusion, fixes the common structure-agnostic PLM experiment and leaves only finite-order non-Gaussian guarantees. Its proof does not contain a transform-zero estimator. \cite{MackeySyrgkanisZadik2018}, Introduction and PLM if-and-only-if theorem, establishes the non-Gaussian second-order moment frontier but not exact location-family annihilation. \cite{DinhGhoshTranTran2021}, quantitative Marcinkiewicz theorem and proof, supplies the bounded zero-free-disk argument adapted to derive \(R_0\). \cite{NeweyRobins2018}, Introduction and split-sample remainder construction, supplies the fold isolation adapted to separate bank selection from final contour evaluation. \cite{ChackoViceira2003}, Introduction and spectral-GMM construction, confirms that complex moments can be stacked as ordinary real GMM restrictions. The closest new 2025 thread, \cite{ReizingerEtAl2025}, proves linear-ICA treatment-effect consistency and explicitly leaves inaccurate-nuisance robustness open; it neither uses observable residual contours nor subsumes the fixed-error risk theorem. For the local candidate, \cite{LeeMesters2024} supplies a weak-non-Gaussian inference template in simultaneous equations, while \cite{DinhGhoshTranTran2021} supplies only one direction between zero-free radius and Gaussian approximation; no paper gives the PLM minimax interpolation. For the inference candidate, \cite{HuShiu2022}, Introduction, isolated-zero asymptotics, and Conclusion, is pointwise on the real axis and expressly distinguishes its results from uniform testing; it does not handle complex contours, multiplicity, learned residuals, or causal studentization. Classical \cite{Mattner1992} remains background: it locates the completeness boundary but does not estimate the PLM coefficient. Thus no adjacent result subsumes the selected kernel.
